newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London welcome election news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London welcome election news.

text.p: U.S. shares rallied strongly in London on Wednesday as U.S. elections delivered the hoped-for Clinton presidential win but with Republicans keeping a firm grip on Congress, traders said.
Worries about a Democrat clean sweep had unsettled markets ahead of the election amid concerns about what such an outcome might have meant for fiscal policy in the U.S.

In the event, Bill Clinton comfortably held onto the White House, the Republicans retained control of the Senate and House of Representatives, lifting hopes that a lid would be kept on government spending.
Bonds and the dollar bounced on the news and Wall Street stocks were also expected to open strongly as fears about a runaway government spending programme faded.
"Stocks are up across the board here in London. Bonds have also rallied and we look set to bounce in New York at the open - maybe 20 or 30 points," said one trader.
Drug stocks were particularly bouyant as concerns about a radical overhaul of the healthcare system also receded.
But dealers were cautious about the prospects of a prolonged leap in share prices and predicted profit-taking would emerge later in the session.

U.S. shares had largely taken the outcome into account, they said, and in the last two sessions had added around 60 points. The Dow, which finished last night at 6,081.18, is just 13 points off its all-time closing high of October 18.

"We don't expect any major impact from the election result. There was quite a rally in bond and equities yesterday and people seemed to be buying on the rumour; they may sell on the news that Republicans have taken Congress," said Merrill Lynch global strategist Trevor Greeton.
"There has been some kind of cross party consensus on things like deficit reduction so there won't be any big change there. The election doesn't change anything in terms of economics."
Stock markets advanced across Europe on the election news with leading shares in London adding over half a percent at one point and breaking a series of disappointing sessions.
German shares also rallied, rising 1-1/2 percent while in France the CAC 40 index rose 21.33 points to 2,208.65.

In the Far East, Japan soared 399.19 points - 1.94 percent - to close at 20,991.52 as the dollar recovered to the 114 yen level and in Hong Kong shares surged 272.77 points to a record high of 12,779.11 as investors welcomed the promise of a stable U.S. economic policy and the prospect of a contining rally in U.S. long bonds.

"The only thing that was preying on people's minds was whether the Republicans would hold onto Congress. The futures and long bond are both trading higher, not as strongly as they were in Asia but they're still ahead," said one London trader.
"We may see shares drift after the inital advance but no sharp profit-taking. There was some degree of position-taking prior to the election but any sell-off should be muted."

As the election dust settles investors attention is likely to quickly return to the health of the U.S. economy with the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting on November 13 the big next hurdle for the market.
